english.notes:
(i) Section 50(2) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 provides that the notification must be made by the person attending at a police station in the person's local police area, and by making an oral notification to a police officer or to a person authorised for the purpose by the officer in charge of the station.
(ii) Section 50(3) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 provided that a person making a notification under section 48 in relation to premises referred to in section 48(3) may make the notification at a police station that would fall within section 48(2)(a) if the address of those premises were the person's home address.
(iii) The notification must be acknowledged in writing, and in such form as the Secretary of State may direct.
(iv) Schedule 4 to the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 makes provision for the application of notification requirements to apply to persons who have been dealt with outside the United Kingdom in respect of a corresponding foreign offence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 54(2) and (2A) of the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
